checks: Source 0b2178fc42ce31d4 §6 states the same planar obstruction and the midpoint interior mechanism. The frozen extension that the whole boundary has zero midpoint mass follows from exactly that mechanism.
At the exposed point each containing halfspace pays the 1/3 atom. An exposing halfspace touches the body only at the point, so its continuous mass is zero and equality holds.

For every other point y, the line through y and v has two closed sides whose continuous masses sum to one. Choose one of mass at most 1/2 and rotate it about y with sign excluding v. Every such rotated closed cap contains y. Dominated convergence on the continuous uniform law and exclusion of the atom give an upper bound of 1/3 on the infimum.

Each endpoint is interior almost surely for any coupling because the full-dimensional convex marginal has a null boundary. Averaging a ball around one endpoint with the other supplies an open neighborhood of the midpoint in (A+B)/2, hence in K. No independence hypothesis is used and no boundary contribution survives.

overlap.comparison: That accepted obstruction has three atoms and comes from an explicit median coupling. It neither computes the uniform-plus-exposed-atom depth nor addresses whether a uniform-endpoint midpoint law can charge a containing body's boundary.
